newsitem.title: CHINA: L'Oreal to boost China investment.
newsitem.headline: L'Oreal to boost China investment.

text.p: France's L'Oreal plans to increase its investment in China in a bid to gain a larger share of China's growing cosmetics market, the Xinhua news agency said.
Construction on L'Oreal's second factory in China began in the eastern city of Suzhou, near Shanghai, this month, it quoted Paolo Gasparrini, general manager of L'Oreal China, as saying.
The first and second phases of the plant are expected to cost more than $40 million.
The first phase is expected to be completed by the end of next year, after which 30 million items can be produced annually, he said in the Xinhua report.
Production capacity of the plant was expected to rise to 150 million items ultimately, he said.

In China, L'Oreal will focus on the barber and beauty shop, and common-use and expensive cosmetic business, he said. L'Oreal China Co has a research centere in Suzhou and training centres in Shanghai and Guangzhou, he said.
L'Oreal faced stiff competition in China from cosmetics firms such as Proctor and Gamble, Estee Lauder, and Avon, Britain's Unilever, and Japan's Shiseido, Gasparrini said.
